Marcus / Ben —

Thanks for the quick handoff call this morning. As discussed, Investra wants a compact MAP we can work against for the next 8 weeks. Primary drivers: minimize customer-facing downtime during migration, ensure two-week canary with rollback gates, and get 8 product ops / support staff trained before launch.

Can you send a draft MAP with:
- target go-live window (preferred weekend windows)
- canary scope (percent of traffic, customer segments)
- migration cutover steps and rollback criteria
- training plan for ops and support (two sessions, TTT recommended)

Also attaching the SOW reference (see DocuSign outstanding items) — we'll need final sign-off on the acceptance criteria before we start cutover rehearsals.

Thanks,

Director, Platform Operations
Investra

Hi Elena —

Appreciate the clear priorities. Attached is a first-pass MAP (Investra_MAP_v1.xlsx) and a short canary runbook stub. High-level summary below — please review and call out changes.

Summary (high level)
- Go-live target window: weekend of May 9–10, 2026 (primary); May 16–17 backup. We picked these to align with your low-traffic weekends and to allow two rehearsals.
- Canary: 10% of traffic for the first 72 hours, expand to 50% after 7 days contingent on error rate < 0.5% and latency delta < 10% vs baseline.
- Migration approach: blue/green with DB shadowing for 48 hrs, DNS cutover with incremental weights. Rollback if error gates trip at any expansion checkpoint.
- Training: two train-the-trainer sessions (remote): Apr 20 and Apr 27. Internal ops shadowing week Apr 27–May 3.
- Acceptance gates: automated smoke suite + customer canonical prompts (we'll provision sample prompts in the MAP).

Action items for Investra:
1) Confirm go-live weekend preference (May 9/10 ok?)
2) Provide list of 10 canonical prompts and 5 support-use cases for acceptance testing
3) Confirm contact roster for TTL and on-call during canary

Attachments: Investra_MAP_v1.xlsx (MAP workbook), Canary_Runbook.pdf (runbook stub)

Next steps: Ben will add migration windows and fallback cadence; Laura will finalize training roster and enrollment links.

Best,
Marcus Lin
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Subject: RE: Implementation drivers & MAP kickoff — migration & canary specifics

Elena / Marcus —

Adding the technical canary/migration details here so the MAP has concrete gates:
- Canary scope: start with 15 medium-value customers (approx. 10% of traffic) routed to the new inference pool. Monitoring: token error ratio, tail latency (95th), and anomaly detector for hallucination rate.
- Metrics & gates: if any one metric exceeds threshold for >15 minutes, autoscale pause + rollback to previous model variant for affected requests.
- Migration windows: three candidate windows (all UTC converted in MAP):
  * Weekend 1: 2026-05-09 02:00–06:00 UTC (primary)
  * Weekend 2: 2026-05-16 02:00–06:00 UTC (backup)
  * Maintenance window: 2026-05-23 02:00–06:00 UTC (buffer)
- DB strategy: dual-write during cutover rehearsal; final cutover uses read-redirect then promote.
- Rollback plan: immediate DNS weight rollback to 0% for new pool + session affinity reset; we keep prior pool warm for 72 hours.

I attached Canary_Runbook.pdf — it has runbook steps, escalation matrix, and the scripts we plan to run for smoke tests.

Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.ai
